HOA & Property Management Website Maintenance · Florida

HOA Website Maintenance in Florida: Keep Your Association Site Compliant, Secure and Current — and Be the Community Owners Find When They Search or Ask AI

This page is for Florida HOA boards, condominium associations and property-management companies whose website is now a legal obligation as well as a front door. Since 1 January 2025 every Florida HOA with 100 or more parcels must maintain an official website or secure portal for its records, and since 1 January 2026 the same applies to condominiums with 25 or more units. A site that is out of date, hacked, or missing a required document is a compliance problem and a trust problem with owners. We keep association websites secure, backed up, fast and current — documents posted on time, owner areas protected, forms delivering — for a flat monthly fee, and we repair what is already broken first. The next step is a free live review of your association’s site.

  • Texas-based since 2013, serving Florida associations remotely; 1,000+ websites repaired
  • Fixes in 2–4 hours, 24/7 support, no upfront payment
  • Maintenance from $300/month per site, month-to-month, cancel with 7 days’ notice
Get a Free Association Site Review
Call 832-266-7209

What the work is aimed at

  1. BaselineWhich required records are posted, which are missing, whether the owner area is actually protected, and whether backups restore.
  2. Repair and hardenFix errors and security gaps; firewall, login protection, least-privilege board and manager accounts.
  3. RhythmA posting workflow with deadlines, staged updates, tested backups, monitoring.
  4. Measured outcomeRecords current, uptime, vulnerabilities closed, backups verified — reported monthly to the board.
On this page
  1. AI search & GEO
  2. Summary
  3. Why association sites fail
  4. Florida requirements
  5. How customers find you
  6. What we improve
  7. How we work
  8. Florida markets we serve
  9. Website structure
  10. Scope and cost
  11. Questions
  12. Start a review

AI search, GEO and AEO

How AI search changes the way owners and buyers find an association — and why a current, readable site now matters for GEO and AEO

Owners, buyers and their lenders no longer work through ten blue links. They ask an assistant for the community’s documents, search the community name on a phone, or ask “who manages [community]?” AI engines only cite sites they can read, trust and reach — a stale or broken association site is skipped. The four searches below show where that happens.

  • Google“[Community name] HOA”The first result should be your official site with the manager’s contact; if it is a third-party directory with wrong data, that is what owners and buyers get.
  • ChatGPT / Gemini“Where are the HOA documents for [community] in Florida?”The assistant points to the official records page if it exists, is reachable and is clearly labelled.
  • Google AI Mode“What are the HOA fees and rules at [community]?”AI answers cite whichever page explains it clearly; an unmaintained site hands that answer to a listing portal.
  • Voice“Hey Google, who manages [community]?”One spoken answer from consistent public data; conflicting manager details give a wrong answer or none.

How it influences the choice

A 2026 study of 24,000 real queries found AI-generated answers on 65% of general-knowledge queries in 2025 and growing across every category. Source: The Rise of AI Search (arXiv, 2026). For an association that means the public page that explains the community, its manager and how to reach the board is increasingly read by a machine first. The site also has to be reachable and current for the assistant to cite it at all — which is a maintenance outcome, not a marketing one.

Why GEO and AEO are important

GEO (generative engine optimisation) is being the source an AI engine cites: consistent community name, address and manager contact everywhere, structured data, clearly labelled public pages. AEO (answer engine optimisation) is writing the public pages so the first paragraph answers the question (what the community is, who manages it, how to reach the board, where owners log in). Both depend on a site that is up, fast, secure and crawlable — what maintenance protects every month.

Owner-only records are never exposed to search or AI engines; GEO/AEO applies to the public pages only.

The short version

What HOA website maintenance in Florida does, and what it cannot promise

What it does: keeps an association or property-management website secure, updated, backed up and online, keeps the owner-only records area protected, and handles the monthly posting of documents, notices, budgets and meeting materials so the site stays current with the statute’s deadlines.

Who it helps: self-managed HOA and condo boards, community association managers, and property-management companies maintaining a portfolio of association sites across Florida.

What changes: documents are posted on time with a log that shows when; owners stop emailing the manager for things that should be online; the board stops worrying about the site being hacked or lost; and a monthly report shows exactly what was done.

What it cannot guarantee: legal compliance — we are a website company, not counsel. We build and maintain the technical system; your attorney confirms what must be posted and when. We also cannot promise a site will never be attacked, only that it is hardened, monitored, backed up and recovered fast.

The problem

Why a Florida association website falls out of compliance without anyone deciding it should

Most association sites were built once by a volunteer or a vendor that has moved on, then left to a manager with twenty other jobs. The failures we see most are predictable:

Required records missing or stale

Last year’s budget, an expired insurance certificate, minutes that stop in March — each a potential statutory gap and an owner complaint.

An owner area that is not really protected

A shared password on a “private” page, documents reachable by direct link, or financials indexed by Google.

Nobody owns the posting workflow

Notices go out by email but not to the site; the 30-day clock on new records runs with no one watching it.

Plugins and themes years out of date

An unmaintained WordPress site holding owner data is exactly what attackers scan for.

Backups never tested

The host “has backups.” No one has restored one. The day the site is hacked or deleted is the day that matters.

Forms that stopped sending

ARB requests, maintenance tickets and contact forms going nowhere for months because a mail setting changed.

Market evidence

What Florida now requires of association websites, and why maintenance is the compliance mechanism

Metric: Florida statutory thresholds requiring a community association to maintain an official website or secure member portal. Scope: Florida. Source: Fla. Stat. § 720.303(4)(b) (homeowners’ associations) and § 718.111(12)(g) (condominium associations), as summarised by Becker and KSN Law (Jan 2026). Method: thresholds and effective dates as published. Limitation: this is a summary for website planning, not legal advice; confirm obligations with association counsel.
Association typeThresholdWebsite required since
Homeowners’ association (Ch. 720)100 or more parcels1 January 2025
Condominium association (Ch. 718)25 or more units (previously 150)1 January 2026
  • The statute lists the official records that must be posted (governing documents, rules, budgets, financial statements, insurance, contracts, board and membership meeting notices and agendas) and requires owner-only records to sit behind a password-protected area, with new items posted within set deadlines. Implication: an HOA site is now a records system with a legal clock on it, not a brochure — maintenance means keeping that system current, secure and recoverable. Source: Becker and KSN Law summaries linked above.
  • The security context is the same as any WordPress site: 11,334 vulnerabilities disclosed in 2025 (+42%), 91% in plugins, 46% unpatched at disclosure, median five hours to mass exploitation. Source: Patchstack, State of WordPress Security in 2026. Implication: an association portal holding owner records and financials needs a firewall, monitoring and tested backups, not just a login form.

How discovery works

Two paths: how owners and buyers reach your site, and how a board finds us

The owner’s and buyer’s path (your association’s funnel)

  • An owner needs a document, a meeting date, an ARB form or a payment link — or a buyer’s lender needs the budget and insurance.
  • They search the community name, follow a link from the manager, or ask an assistant “where are the [community] HOA documents?”
  • The site has to load, the owner login has to work, and the document has to be the current one.
  • Forms and tickets have to reach the manager; payments have to reach the right processor.
  • Any failure becomes a phone call to the manager, a records request, or a complaint.

The owner’s path (our funnel, so you know how we think)

  • A board member or manager inherits a site nobody maintains, or receives a records request the site should have answered.
  • They search “HOA website maintenance Florida” or ask an assistant who maintains association websites.
  • They read this page, see real prices and a real business, and want the site looked at rather than a pitch.
  • They request a live review; we share a screen and show what is missing, exposed or broken.
  • We measure our own work by qualified consultations, exactly as we measure your site’s uptime and records currency.

This page is written for boards and managers. We are a website maintenance and repair company, not a law firm or a management company; statutory obligations are confirmed by your association’s counsel.

What we improve

Six things an association maintenance plan actually changes

A records area built for the statute

Deliverables: a structured, searchable documents library with the categories the statute names, a protected owner-only area, and a posting log that records what went up and when.

Why: the site is now a records system with deadlines.

Limit: what must be posted is confirmed by your attorney; we build and run the system.

Security hardening and monitoring

Deliverables: firewall, login protection, least-privilege accounts for board and manager, file-change and uptime monitoring, vulnerability watch on every component.

Why: owner data and financials make an association site a target.

Limit: no system is unhackable; we reduce exposure and respond fast.

Staged updates with rollback

Deliverables: core, plugin and theme updates tested on a copy first and rolled back automatically if anything breaks.

Why: an untested update is the most common cause of a dead site.

Backups that are actually restorable

Deliverables: daily off-site backups with retention and a monthly test restore.

Why: years of records cannot be recreated.

Monthly posting and content changes

Deliverables: meeting notices, agendas, minutes, budgets, insurance and contracts posted within the plan; forms, calendars and announcements updated.

Why: currency is the whole point of the requirement.

Board-ready reporting

Deliverables: a monthly report of records posted, uptime, vulnerabilities closed, backups verified, changes made and incidents.

Why: the board should be able to show diligence.

How we work toward the goal

The association maintenance flow, with the decisions built in

  1. Establish the goal and baselineConfirm with counsel which records apply; inventory what is posted, missing, exposed or stale; record uptime, speed and backup status.
  2. Audit and inventoryPlugins, themes, users, forms, payment and portal integrations, hosting and DNS.
  3. Repair what is broken nowErrors, exposed documents, dead forms, malware — fixed first, usually within 2–4 hours.
  4. Harden and reduceFirewall, login protection, least-privilege accounts, unused plugins removed, PHP supported.
  5. Build the records workflowCategories, owner-only area, posting checklist with deadlines, and who sends us what each month.
  6. Keep the site findableThe community name, address and manager contact consistent everywhere; sitemaps and redirects intact after every change.
  7. Monthly posting and changesDocuments, notices and announcements posted on schedule with a log.
  8. MeasureMonthly report to the board: records currency, uptime, security, backups, changes.
  9. RefineAdjust the workflow to what the report shows.
  10. Feedback loopSteps 7–9 repeat monthly; steps 3–6 reopen whenever monitoring or counsel points back at them.

Decision points

  • If owner documents are publicly reachableLock the area, rotate links, request de-indexing and notify the board before any routine work.
  • If a required record is missingFlag it to the manager with the deadline; we post what we are sent, we do not create association records.
  • If the site is compromisedClean, restore from a verified backup, rotate every credential, close the entry point.
  • Optional branch: redesign or new portalQuoted separately when the current site cannot be made compliant or usable.

Florida markets

Where in Florida we maintain association and property-management sites, and what differs by market

We serve Florida associations remotely from Texas with 24/7 support. The markets below are where our Florida work concentrates; the statute is statewide, but the practical pressures differ.

  • SE FLMiami-Dade, Broward, Palm BeachDense condo market; the 25-unit 2026 threshold brought thousands of small associations into the requirement; bilingual owner communication.
  • SW FLNaples, Fort Myers, SarasotaLarge HOA communities and seasonal owners who rely on the portal while away; storm-season uptime.
  • C FLOrlando, TampaFast-growing master-planned HOAs crossing the 100-parcel line as they build out.
  • NE FLJacksonville, St. AugustineMixed HOA and condo portfolios managed by regional management companies.
  • PMProperty-management portfoliosOne maintenance standard across every association site, with a report per association for each board.
  • SELFSelf-managed boardsVolunteer boards that need the workflow done for them, not a tool to learn.

How we scope a plan: by association type and size against the statutory threshold, the number of records categories in use, whether payments or a portal are integrated, and how many sites a management company runs. We do not claim a Florida office; Florida information on this page applies to Florida associations only, and legal obligations are confirmed by your counsel.

Content and website architecture

What a compliant, maintainable association website looks like

1

Public area

Community name and address, manager contact, amenities, public notices, how to reach the board — consistent with Google and directories.

2

Owner-only records area

Password-protected library organised by the statute’s categories, searchable, with posting dates visible.

3

Forms, calendar, payments

ARB requests, maintenance tickets, meeting calendar and payment links that are tested monthly.

4

Backups, staging, logs

Off-site backups, a staging copy for updates, and an activity log so every posting has a who and a when.

A compliant site is mostly a current site. The workflow — who sends what, by when — matters more than the design.

Scope, timing and investment

What is included, what it depends on, and what moves the cost

Included in an association maintenance plan

  • Records library and owner-only area kept current and protected
  • Security hardening, firewall and monitoring
  • Staged updates with rollback; daily backups with monthly test restore
  • Monthly posting of documents, notices and announcements
  • Forms, calendar and payment links tested monthly
  • Monthly board-ready report and posting log

Dependencies and timing

Repairs are usually done within 2–4 hours. The first month covers the audit, hardening and the records workflow; from the second month, posting runs on the association’s calendar. Building a records area for a site that has none is quoted separately and typically completed within the first month.

What affects cost

Number of sites, whether a records area already exists, how many documents are posted each month, and whether payments or a portal are integrated. Maintenance starts at $300 per month per site; one-off fixes start at $50; hacked-site repair is $200. No upfront payment — you pay after the work is done — and plans are month-to-month, cancellable with 7 days’ notice. A new records area or full redesign is quoted separately.

Proof and expertise

What you can verify about us before a call

Since 2013

Fix Website Issues is a DBA of Bizzsol LLC, a Texas-registered business based in Houston, serving all 50 states.

1,000+ websites repaired

Repair is our origin and still our most common job; 2–4 hours is the typical fix time and support is 24/7.

500+ websites designed or redesigned

Counted separately from repairs, across WordPress and headless WordPress.

Pay after the fix

$0 upfront. We show you the live errors first, fix them, and you pay when it works.

We publish client results only with the client’s permission, a stated timeframe, a baseline and the measurement method. Where that permission has not been given, we show our process instead of inventing numbers.

Questions boards and managers ask

HOA website maintenance in Florida: direct answers

Does our association actually need a website?

Under Florida law, HOAs with 100 or more parcels have needed an official website or secure portal since 1 January 2025, and condominiums with 25 or more units since 1 January 2026. Smaller associations are not required to, though many choose to. Confirm your specific obligation with your association’s attorney; we build and maintain the site, we do not give legal advice.

What has to be on it?

The statutes list the records: governing documents and rules, budgets and financial reports, insurance, contracts, board and membership meeting notices and agendas, among others, with owner-only items behind a password. Your counsel confirms the list for your association; we build the library around it and post what the manager sends us, on time, with a log.

Can we use a Facebook group or a free page builder?

A social media group does not meet the requirement, and most free builders cannot protect owner-only records properly or keep a posting log. A maintained WordPress site or a purpose-built portal can. We will tell you plainly which fits your size and budget.

What is included in $300 a month?

Security hardening and monitoring, staged updates with rollback, daily backups with a monthly test restore, the owner-only records area kept protected, monthly posting of the documents and notices the manager sends, forms and payment links tested, and a board-ready report. Building a records area where none exists, or a redesign, is quoted separately.

Our site was built by a former board member — can you take it over?

Yes, most association sites we maintain were built by someone else. We start with the audit: what is posted, what is exposed, what is broken. If the site cannot be made compliant and secure at reasonable cost we will say so and quote a rebuild instead.

Do you manage the association or send the notices?

No. We maintain the website and post what the manager or board sends us. Management, legal notice content and statutory interpretation stay with your manager and attorney. That separation keeps everyone’s responsibilities clear.

How do you handle owner data and privacy?

Owner-only records sit behind authenticated access with least-privilege accounts, the site is firewalled and monitored, backups are encrypted off-site, and we never place owner data in analytics or third-party tools. We cannot promise no attack will ever succeed; we can promise it is hardened, watched and recoverable.

What can you control, and what can’t you?

We control security posture, update discipline, backup integrity, posting on time once we have the documents, and response speed. We do not control what counsel says must be posted, when the manager sends it, your host’s outages, or a brand-new zero-day; what we control is how quickly and cleanly the site recovers.

Start with a free association site review

A screen-shared session where we check what is posted, what is exposed, what is broken, and whether backups restore — and show you exactly what we found. No upfront charge, no obligation.

What to have ready

  • Your association’s website address and who hosts it
  • Roughly how many parcels or units you have
  • Who currently posts documents, and any attorney guidance you have on what must be posted

What happens next: we run the live review, send a short written list of findings, and quote repairs, any records-area build and the monthly plan separately. Plans are month-to-month with no upfront payment; cancel with 7 days’ notice.
